reviews.title: Terrible, Overpriced
reviews.text:
I downloaded the app after starting a story on FB. I wasn’t sure how it would work, but what I ran into after finishing the free chapters was outrageous. 
It’s ridiculous to have varying “coin” amounts per chapter and even more worthless to earn nowhere near enough to finish a single chapter through ads. I never saw a possibility of a subscription for unlimited reading and purchasing coins doesn’t guarantee you’ll get enough to finish the story. Not to mention the cost is way overpriced for a single “book” when compared with purchasing a book from book stores.

There is no monthly/annual subscription fee option and to download all the chapters of the book that I’m trying to read takes around 2000 Turkish Lira. reviews.title: Too Expensive
reviews.text:
I recently started using your app. I think it is a great platform for supporting new and aspiring writers, but your excessive pricing policy is quite frustrating.

It is very difficult to earn coins and bonuses through the tasks, while the rewards are quite low. On top of that, each chapter requires a large number of coins, even though the chapters themselves are very short. As a result, finishing a single book can end up costing four or five times more than buying a traditionally published book.

For relatively unknown Wattpad authors, this is an incredibly high price to pay.

I think there should be an option for a monthly subscription. The amount of coins and bonuses that users can earn should also be increased, and the overall pricing system should be reconsidered. The amount of coins offered in exchange for real money is also far too low.

There are so many stories and so many aspiring writers on the platform. If the prices were more reasonable, I believe more people would actually read these stories, and more writers would have the opportunity to gain readers and support.

I will probably finish the book I am currently reading because I am already too invested in it, but under these conditions, I don’t want to continue using the app.

I hope you will take this feedback into consideration.

reviews.title: $65+ for one book?
reviews.text:
Stories (based on reading the free preview chapters) are pretty good. You can get about 12 short chapters into a story before you need coins to unlock more. Based on how much coins cost, and including a bonus of 2400 coins for buying a 6500 coin pack, it would cost me $65 to read a single 200 chapter book in this app. One book. ONE. For $65. For that price I can go online or to local Barnes & Noble and buy four $15 paperbacks. Or pay for almost five months of Kindle Unlimited where I can read 20 books at any given time, and this includes releases of best sellers like Fourth Wing.  I have a couple other e-book apps for new/amateur authors to publish their stories. These apps are one set monthly or yearly fee for every book in their catalogue. If this app offered unlimited books for $65 per year for a full, unlimited subscription I’d have no issues. 

Don’t fall for the promise of free reading full books in this app when all you get is 10-12 chapters and then they want $65 in climax

reviews.title: Rip Off
reviews.text: I am a fairly new user of this app. I love reading and this app has novels on it that I can’t find anywhere else. I make sure to check in daily for bonuses and points. I mad the mistake of purchasing points and I have used all of them on a novel that I would love so much to finish reading but that is not going to happen after this review. So after I used all of my points and continued to check in daily I am now no longer getting points/bonuses. It seems like once you start spending your own money you stop getting daily points/bonuses. I have been checking in for the last two or three days and it says you’ve received your daily points or bonuses but there is nothing other than the few points or bonuses that I already had which in fact is enough to unlock another chapter but I also haven’t been able to do that either. I just want to say I hope that little twenty dollars was worth it because I’m done. I have other apps that I have had for years without these issues. I’m just glad that this happened early on verses waiting until I have spent enough to buy the whole book or a few books. This app had potential but not now. Going back to my favorites.

reviews.title: Frustrating beyond words
reviews.text:
Deeply frustrating,
Chapters are short and the hoops you have to jump through to read further chapters are ridiculous. 
If you have t been suckered into “subscribing” - at eye wateringly expensive subscription rates, then you’re “earning” your next chapter hit by watch ads/read articles on the web to gather enough bonuses/coins to pay for the next chapter. Each chapter shows a bonus/coin “price” to read it - once you’ve used up your bonus, you’d think the next chapter would open because you’ve gather sufficient coins - but it doesn’t . 
There’s no information on how to exchange the coins for chapters so really what the h*ll are they there for? In fact, there’s no information anywhere about how the site works.
I’d rather the chapters were time released so you knew you’d get a couple of chapters each day and then if you’re enjoying it you could earn “opening” credits to read on, and for them to be reset with a count down clock like other apps do. 

How do you exchange your coins for chapters? 
Why is the subscription charge so high. 

Other apps do this SO much better. 
Tempted to dump the app altogether. 
Deeply frustrating - do MUCH better Stary!

reviews.title: Don’t download
reviews.text: I’m over 100 chapters in my first and only book I plan to read on this app. I like the story, therefore I’m invested. However, free is an illusion that they sell / advertise to you. It is NOT free. At this point I would rather an option of an outright purchase of the entire book. Because I’m bleeding ever so many chapters. I tried the free route of watching a few videos and clicking through “read 2 or 3 advertisements” just to pick up only a few bonus coins. But you need at least over 50 for 1 chapter. So after a while I break down spend $9.99 for several chapters. I’ve already done this 3 times. $30 dollars and 100 plus chapters later and they want more coins or more money and I have zero clue “how” many chapters are even in the book? I’m very, very, very angry!!! No out right bookstore purchase would cost this much - maybe for a hardback or rare book. There should be a spending cap on a book where your purchased coins would be saved for another book and the remainder of your book is free to read. Definitely no more than $20 but since advertised “free” it should be $10. They are just being greedy!!

reviews.title: Extortionate pricing
reviews.text:
You get lured in with several chapters, but then have to pay ridiculous amounts to have access to the next chapters - of which there are like 150! It cost me £23 just to get through the first 65 chapters. 

You can pay £6.99 for 10 ‘episodes’. This supposedly gives you 700+ credits. You then use 500 credits for 10 episodes, only to find at the end of them you only have around 40 credits left instead of the 200 you should have? The whole credit system doesn’t make sense or add up at all. If I want to finish the book I’m reading (which is good, but FULL of spelling mistakes, grammatical errors and poor editing), it’ll probably end up costing me around £60. And nobody in their right mind is going to pay £60 for a book, (when in a normal bookstore they’re around £10-£15 max). Especially for one that’s so poorly written and edited. 

CHANGE YOUR PRICING STRUCTURE AND STOP RIPPING PEOPLE OFF!!
